svg.title: Security filter chain
svg.desc: The ordered WebFilter chain on Laravel's global middleware stack — the two prepended framework filters, tracing, HTTP exchanges and metrics, security headers, session context persistence, logout, the five authentication mechanisms, the OAuth2 client and authorization-server filters, CSRF and the deny-by-default URL rules — with each filter's real #[Order] value, and the DelegatingAuthenticationEntryPoint that decides between a login redirect, a Basic challenge and a 401.
svg.text: The security filter chain: every filter, in the order the registrar sorts it
packages/web/src/Filter/{FilterChainRegistrar.php, RequestContextFilter.php, CorrelationIdFilter.php} · packages/observability/src/Web/{TracingFilter.php, HttpExchangeFilter.php, MetricsFilter.php}
packages/security/src/{Web,Web/Basic,Web/Login,Web/Logout,Web/RememberMe,Web/EntryPoint,Session,OAuth2}/*.php
packages/security-oauth2-client/src/Web/*.php · packages/security-oauth2-server/src/Web/OAuth2AuthorizationServerFilter.php
Laravel's global middleware stack · FilterChainRegistrar::orderedFilters()

HSTS, CSP, frame, nosniff and referrer headers

svg.text: ControllerDispatcher → the #[RestController] action
MethodSecurityControllerGuard enforces a controller's own #[PreAuthorize] here, at dispatch
DelegatingAuthenticationEntryPoint
firefly.security.http.entry_point · default auto

g.text: names text/html, is neither an XHR nor a wantsJson() call,
and its path is not in firefly.web.error-page.json-paths —
is sent to the login page when form login or OAuth2 login
is on; else a Basic challenge when HTTP Basic is on; else
always the login page — refused at boot when neither
form login nor OAuth2 login is enabled.
always the exception, rendered by firefly/web.

svg.text: prefersHtml(), never handles(): error-page.enabled is a branding
choice and must never decide whether a person is asked to sign in.
Reached from HttpSecurityFilter's anonymous denial, and from the
authorization server's /oauth2/authorize. HttpBasicFilter answers
with BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint instead — never this one, because
a caller that presented Basic has already chosen its mechanism.
How the order is decided

g.text: orderedFilters() sorts every WebFilter bean by its
ComponentDescriptor::$order — the manifest's number, never a
resolved instance's — and breaks ties with strcmp on the class
name, which is why HttpExchangeFilter precedes MetricsFilter at
the same -100. RequestContextFilter and CorrelationIdFilter are
PREPENDED: they carry no #[Order] and are never sorted.

svg.text: What is NOT in this chain

g.text: #[PreAuthorize] on a controller action is enforced at dispatch by
#[PreAuthorize] on any OTHER stereotyped bean is enforced by
MethodSecurityInterceptor inside that bean's own proxy.
A filter whose package is not installed, or whose
A WebFilter produced by a #[Bean] method is not discovered:
orderedFilters() matches on the COMPONENT class only.

svg.text: Every DISCOVERED filter extends OncePerRequestFilter and is an ordinary #[Component] behind at least one #[ConditionalOnProperty]: installing a package
adds its link, and switching the feature off removes it. Nothing here is a hard-coded list — only the two prepended framework filters are unconditional.
Order values are the literal #[Order(...)] arguments on the classes named; they are the contract a WebFilter of your own inserts itself against.
